A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Mirai research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, and figures, are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet generation experiments, training comparisons, component ablations, and representation visualizations for Mirai.

after.justification: v2 reports original Mirai experiments, including retained ImageNet results and additional evaluations of larger models and limited-data training.

M1.justification: The Mirai-E EMA encoder, Mirai-I frozen bidirectional encoder, representation alignment objectives, projection heads, and causal inference procedure remain unchanged. The additional model scales do not introduce a new Mirai procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate ImageNet class-conditional image generation, including the existing 256×256 and 384×384 settings. v2's reduced-data experiment changes sample quantity within ImageNet, without introducing a new dataset, population, or task.

E2.justification: Table 6 retains the same comparator methods, and the PAR comparison is preserved. The new S and XXL experiments use size configurations of the existing LlamaGen baseline. MuToR is discussed as related work but is not added to an evaluated comparison.

E3.justification: v2 adds LlamaGen-XXL at 1.4B parameters trained for 40 epochs and LlamaGen-S trained for 80 epochs with 100 ImageNet images per class on one A100 GPU (Tables 12 and 14). These extend the experimental settings; the existing protocols and metrics are retained.

E4.justification: Appendix K and Figure 10 add failure-case analysis showing object/background or neighboring-object merging with 16 foresight tokens. v1 already tested this token count in Figure 4. Likewise, the current-only condition added to Table 5 corresponds to the existing K=1 experiment, rather than an entirely new ablation.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical tests for these experiments. The additional results follow the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: v2 adds XXL FIDs of 3.49/3.04/3.10 and limited-data S FIDs of 47.81/35.62/41.84, ordered baseline/Mirai-I/Mirai-E (Tables 12 and 14). These are comparisons under newly reported settings, not changes to earlier scores. Table 5 also adds IS 182.19 for current-only Mirai-E; the original benchmark values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–11, the formal foresight definitions, neighborhood rules, and loss formulations are retained. Added intuitive explanations and conjectures do not introduce or revise mathematical derivations or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: two foresight variants, unchanged inference cost, faster convergence, and improved generation quality. The headline 10× acceleration and FID reduction from 5.34 to 4.34 are unchanged.

C2.justification: v1 discusses excessive foresight mainly through conflicting gradients and worsening FID. v2's Appendix K adds a concrete limitation: excessive foresight can merge objects with their surroundings, potentially through over-constraining representations and compromising locality. It identifies reducing foresight as mitigation.

D1.justification: v2 documents that LlamaGen-S halves LlamaGen-B's parameters and uses 100 images per class with a single A100 GPU. It also specifies the added XXL model's parameter count and training budget. Existing optimizer, projector, EMA, sampling details, and the project-page link are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 adds MuToR and explains how register tokens alleviate quality degradation in multi-token prediction. The existing positioning relative to REPA and other approaches remains substantially unchanged. Other reference changes include publication metadata updates rather than additional research works.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized grammar and prose revisions in the abstract, introduction, and method explanation. It adds acknowledgments, an ethics paragraph, and short appendix sections while retaining the main section sequence and most existing text.

P2.justification: v2 adds two results tables and the failure-case Figure 10, expands and reorders Table 5, and adjusts figure sizes and page flow. Existing PAR/FLOP tables and qualitative sample grids are retained with relocation or renumbering; the overall visual design remains stable.

improvement.justification: The added XXL and limited-data comparisons provide targeted support for applicability beyond the earlier configurations. Appendix K and Figure 10 make an excessive-foresight failure mode concrete, improving transparency about limitations. These are useful incremental gains while the method, principal results, and central conclusions remain unchanged.
